value.summary: No open PR was found for branch `Main`; `git diff main...HEAD` was empty, `master` was unavailable, and `git diff HEAD~1` was non-empty only outside the requested scope. The review scope is therefore the untracked `apps/app` Astro/Svelte rewrite files only, excluding ignored generated/dependency output such as `apps/app/dist`, `apps/app/.astro`, and `apps/app/node_modules`; focus review on runtime blockers in Astro routing/layouts, Svelte component wiring, Convex client usage, and Clerk/auth wiring, not root/mobile/archive/package churn outside `apps/app`.
value.conventions: Root AGENTS.md: Convex backend work must follow `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md`. Convex guidelines read: use generated `api` references, validators on Convex functions, and current Convex calling patterns. `apps/app/AGENTS.md`: run Astro dev server with `astro dev --background`; use Astro docs for routing, components, framework components, content, styling, and i18n. `apps/app/README.md` is the default Astro minimal starter README with `bun dev/build/preview/astro` commands.

candidates.summary: Clerk boot failures are launched with `void initAuth()` and leave auth stuck loading with an unhandled rejection.
candidates.impact: If Clerk's script/load call rejects due to network, bad key, or blocked third-party resources, the app never sets `authState.ready`, stays on the loading/auth path, and the rejected promise is only reported globally.

candidates.summary: Offline food saves are queued but immediately followed by an online query, producing an unhandled failure after the optimistic update.
candidates.impact: When `runMutation` queues `logs.foodLogs.setDay` offline, `loadDay()` still queries Convex; that query fails offline, so Add/remove food handlers reject while the UI has already mutated `foodEntries` locally.

candidates.summary: Offline water saves queue the mutation then still reload the day from Convex.
candidates.impact: Clicking water quick-add while offline stores an offline mutation, then `loadDay()` rejects; the button handler has no catch, causing an unhandled error and leaving the user unsure whether the queued write succeeded.

candidates.summary: Queue flush swallows the first replay error and gives no signal for permanently bad queued items.
candidates.impact: A validation/schema error or stale mutation name during offline replay is caught and ignored with `break`, leaving that item at the front of localStorage forever and blocking all later queued mutations without any visible error.

candidates.summary: Progress photo upload does not check upload response success before saving the measurement.
candidates.impact: If the storage upload returns a non-OK response or JSON without `storageId`, the code proceeds to `bodyProgress.save` without the photo, silently creating a partial progress record instead of surfacing the upload failure.

candidates.summary: Settings are saved with parallel independent mutations, so one failure can leave preferences partially updated.
candidates.impact: If one settings mutation rejects after others have already committed, the app has persisted only part of the settings form; the rejected handler is uncaught and no rollback or clear partial-save state is shown.

candidates.summary: Saving an active workout repeatedly double-counts elapsed time because the accumulated elapsed value is added to time since the original start on every update.
candidates.impact: Each set/rep/checkbox change persists an inflated elapsedSeconds; finishing later can record workout durations far longer than real time.

candidates.summary: Offline-queued food changes immediately call loadDay, so the queued mutation path still performs network reads while offline.
candidates.impact: Adding/removing food offline queues the mutation, then loadDay fails against Convex, leaving an error/unhandled rejection instead of a clean offline save.

candidates.summary: Offline-queued water changes immediately call loadDay, so the queued mutation path still performs network reads while offline.
candidates.impact: Adding water offline queues the write but then tries to refetch the day, causing the offline action to surface as a failure despite being queued.

candidates.summary: Client navigation only pushes history and never handles popstate, so browser Back/Forward changes the URL without updating the rendered view.
candidates.impact: After navigating inside the app, using browser Back can leave the URL on one route while currentView still renders the previous screen, breaking routing state.

candidates.summary: Concurrent food log writes replace the whole day from stale client snapshots, so rapid add/remove actions can drop entries.
candidates.impact: Two overlapping calls such as double-clicking Add food or logging a search result while removing another entry both send full-day `entries`; the slower mutation can overwrite the faster one and lose food logs.

candidates.summary: Day navigation has no stale-response guard, so rapid previous/next clicks can show one date with another date’s data.
candidates.impact: If an earlier `loadDay()` resolves after a later navigation, `foodEntries`, water, supplements, and workout state are overwritten with the wrong day while `dateKey` remains on the latest date.

candidates.summary: Offline queue flushing can run concurrently and replay the same queued mutations twice.
candidates.impact: `online` and `loadEverything()` can both enter `flushQueue()` with the same localStorage snapshot; non-idempotent queued mutations like water entries or supplement logs can be duplicated.

candidates.summary: Clerk SignIn is mounted without a Svelte action destroy hook, leaking the mounted Clerk UI when the login branch unmounts.
candidates.impact: After sign-in or route changes, Clerk’s mounted widget/listeners can remain attached to a detached DOM node, causing leaked observers and duplicate auth UI work on later mounts.

candidates.summary: Progress photo upload ignores failed or empty upload responses and can silently save the measurement without the selected photo.
candidates.impact: On expired upload URLs, 413s, or JSON responses without `storageId`, the code continues to save progress with no `photoStorageId`, losing the user’s photo without an error.

candidates.summary: The route allow-list is duplicated between `allowedViews` and `getStaticPaths`.
candidates.impact: When a view is added or removed, updating only one list either generates a route that falls back to `today` or allows a view that Astro never statically builds; derive `getStaticPaths()` from `allowedViews`.

candidates.summary: The offline queue adds a parallel string-to-mutation registry instead of calling the generated Convex refs directly.
candidates.impact: Every queued mutation now needs a second entry in `mutationRefs`; a missing or renamed key turns into `undefined` at flush time and the queue remains stuck behind the bad item.

candidates.summary: `env` is imported but never used.
candidates.impact: This leaves a dead Convex/Clerk configuration path in the main component, so future config changes can be made against an import that has no runtime effect.

candidates.summary: Navigation intercepts Astro links with `history.pushState` but never handles `popstate`.
candidates.impact: Back/forward buttons change the URL without updating `currentView`, leaving the Svelte UI on the wrong page until a full reload; this bypasses Astro's normal routing behavior.
candidates.recommendation: Either let the `<a href>` perform normal Astro navigation or add a minimal `popstate` handler that derives `currentView` from `location.pathname`.

candidates.summary: The app dev script does not follow the scoped convention to run Astro with `--background`.
candidates.impact: Tooling or agents following the project convention can start `bun dev` and block indefinitely instead of getting a background Astro server for runtime verification.
candidates.recommendation: Change the dev script to `astro dev --background` if this package script is the intended entrypoint.

evidence: `saveFoodEntries` optimistically updates local state, then always reloads after the mutation: `foodEntries = entries; await runMutation("logs.foodLogs.setDay", { date: dateKey, entries }); await loadDay();` (apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:498-501).
`runMutation` queues instead of mutating when offline: `if (!navigator.onLine && options.queue) { enqueueMutation(name, args); return null; }` (apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:464-467).

`loadDay` performs Convex reads via `query(...)`, including food logs: `const [goalsRes, foods, water, supplements, log, active] = await Promise.all([ query(api.users.users.getEffectiveGoals, { date: dateKey }), query(api.logs.foodLogs.getDay, { date: dateKey }), ... ])` (apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:367-374).

Food add/remove routes through `saveFoodEntries`: `await saveFoodEntries([...foodEntries, entry]);` and `await saveFoodEntries(foodEntries.filter((entry) => entry.id !== id));` (apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:517, 523).

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:367-374: `async function loadDay() {
    const [goalsRes, foods, water, supplements, log, active] = await Promise.all([
      query(api.users.users.getEffectiveGoals, { date: dateKey }),
      query(api.logs.foodLogs.getDay, { date: dateKey }),
      query(api.logs.water.getDay, { date: dateKey }),`

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:948-956: `async function saveActive(active: AnyRecord, rows: AnyRecord[]) { ... await runMutation("logs.activeWorkout.updateActive", { ... elapsedSeconds: elapsedSeconds(active), }); await loadDay(); }`

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:960-963: `function elapsedSeconds(active: AnyRecord) { const started = toNum(active.startedAt, Date.now()); return Math.max(0, Math.round((Date.now() - started) / 1000) + toNum(active.elapsedSeconds)); }`

convex/logs/activeWorkout.ts:160-164: `await ctx.db.patch(active._id, { items: args.items, exerciseData: args.exerciseData, elapsedSeconds: args.elapsedSeconds, });` — `startedAt` is not reset when the accumulated `elapsedSeconds` is patched, so the next save adds the prior persisted elapsed to time since the original start again.
`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:79` initializes local route state once: `let currentView = initialView;`

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:407-410` only updates state when the app's own navigate handler runs: `function navigate(view: View) { currentView = view; history.pushState({}, "", routeFor(view)); }`
`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1119-1120` intercepts nav links with `href={routeFor(view.id)}` and `on:click|preventDefault={() => navigate(view.id)}`.
No `popstate` handler exists in `OneRepApp.svelte`; the only window listeners in `onMount` are `online` and `offline`, removed in cleanup.

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:213-219 subscribes to authState and only clears loading when `value.ready` is true: `if (value.ready && value.signedIn && loadedUserId !== value.userId) { ... }` and `if (value.ready && !value.signedIn) loading = false;`.
apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:229 launches auth without handling failures: `void initAuth();`.
apps/app/src/lib/convex.ts:24 initializes auth as not ready: `export const authState = writable<AuthState>({ ready: false, signedIn: false });`.

apps/app/src/lib/convex.ts:51-56 awaits Clerk load with no catch/finally before setting ready: `clerk = new Clerk(clerkKey); await clerk.load({ ... });`; `syncAuth()` setting `ready: true` is only called later at lines 68-69.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:481-493`: `async function flushQueue() { ... const remaining = [...items]; for (const item of items) { try { await mutate(mutationRefs[item.name] as any, item.args as never); remaining.shift(); writeQueue(remaining); } catch { break; } }` — on any replay error, the failing item is not shifted/written out and the loop stops.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:453-459`: `function writeQueue(...) { localStorage.setItem(queueKey(), JSON.stringify(queueItems)); ... }` and `enqueueMutation(...) { writeQueue([...readQueue(), { name, args }]); ... }` — queued mutations persist in localStorage, so a permanently failing first item remains at the front.
`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:491-492`: `} catch { break; }` — the error is swallowed with no `handleError`, toast, or rethrow.

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1017-1024 uploads the file and immediately parses JSON/assigns `uploaded.storageId` without checking `res.ok` or validating the field: `const res = await fetch(uploadUrl, { ... }); const uploaded = await res.json(); photoStorageId = uploaded.storageId;`

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1026-1035 then always calls `await runMutation("bodyProgress.save", { ... ...(photoStorageId ? { photoStorageId } : {}), });`, so an undefined/missing `storageId` is omitted and the progress record is still saved.
convex/bodyProgress.ts:47-59 declares `photoStorageId: v.optional(v.id("_storage"))`, confirming the save mutation accepts records without a photo.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1056-1066` defines `async function saveSettings()` and immediately `await Promise.all([` over eight separate `runMutation(...)` calls: `setCustomGoals`, `setWaterGoal`, `setWeightUnit`, `setDashboardSettings`, `setMacroCycling`, `setWorkoutAdjustment`, `setPrivacySettings`, and `setPushReminders`.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:468-476` shows `runMutation` rethrows non-network errors: `throw err;`, so a failed mutation rejects the `Promise.all` while any already-committed sibling mutations are not rolled back.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1593` invokes it as `<button class="button primary" on:click={() => void saveSettings()}>Save settings</button>`, with no local catch/error state around the rejected promise.

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:502-505: `async function saveFoodEntries(entries: AnyRecord[]) {` / `foodEntries = entries;` / `await runMutation("logs.foodLogs.setDay", { date: dateKey, entries });` / `await loadDay();` — each save sends a whole-day `entries` array and reloads after the async mutation.

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:520: `await saveFoodEntries([...foodEntries, entry]);` and 525-526: `async function removeFood(id: string) { await saveFoodEntries(foodEntries.filter((entry) => entry.id !== id)); }` — add/remove compute replacement arrays from the current client `foodEntries`, so overlapping setDay mutations can overwrite each other by arrival order.
apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:611-613: `async function logFoodResult... await saveFoodEntries([ ...foodEntries,` — search-result logging uses the same full-day replacement path.

`previousDay` and `nextDay` mutate the shared `dateKey` and then start `loadDay()` without any request token/date snapshot guard: `412 async function previousDay() { 413 dateKey = offsetDateKey(dateKey, -1); 414 await loadDay(); }` and `417 async function nextDay() { 418 dateKey = offsetDateKey(dateKey, 1); 419 await loadDay(); }`

`loadDay()` queries using the current `dateKey`, then unconditionally writes results after the await: `367 async function loadDay() { 368 const [goalsRes, foods, water, supplements, log, active] = await Promise.all([ 369 query(... { date: dateKey }), ... ]); 377 effectiveGoals = goalsRes; 378 foodEntries = foods ?? []; 379 waterEntries = water ?? []; 380 supplementOverview = supplements ?? emptySupplementOverview(); 381 workoutLog = log;`
The UI fires these async navigations without disabling/serializing them: `1137 <button on:click={() => void previousDay()}>←</button>` and `1139 <button on:click={() => void nextDay()}>→</button>`.
apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:222-224: `const markOnline = () => { offline = false; void flushQueue(); };`
apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:315-317: `await Promise.all([loadStaticData(), loadDay()]); await flushQueue();`

apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:481-490: `async function flushQueue() { ... const items = readQueue(); ... const remaining = [...items]; for (const item of items) { await mutate(...); remaining.shift(); writeQueue(remaining); }` — there is no in-flight guard/lock, and the queue is only rewritten after each awaited mutation.
apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:750-752 and 814-816 show queued non-set operations: `runMutation("logs.water.addEntry", ...)` and `runMutation(... "logs.supplements.logTaken", ...)`.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1018-1024`: `const res = await fetch(uploadUrl, { ... }); const uploaded = await res.json(); photoStorageId = uploaded.storageId;` — there is no `res.ok` check or validation that `storageId` exists.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1026-1034`: `await runMutation("bodyProgress.save", { ... ...(photoStorageId ? { photoStorageId } : {}), });` — if `uploaded.storageId` is missing/undefined, the save still runs and omits the photo.

`apps/app/src/pages/[view].astro:5-16` defines `const allowedViews = [ "foods", "workouts", "active-workout", "water", "supplements", "progress", "exercises", "settings", "onboarding", "login" ] as const;`

`apps/app/src/pages/[view].astro:19-32` repeats the same literals inside `getStaticPaths()`: `return [ "foods", "workouts", "active-workout", "water", "supplements", "progress", "exercises", "settings", "onboarding", "login" ].map((view) => ({ params: { view } }));`
`apps/app/src/pages/[view].astro:35` uses only `allowedViews` for runtime validation: `const initialView = (allowedViews.includes(raw as (typeof allowedViews)[number]) ? raw : "today") as View;`

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1095-1106`: login branch renders `{@render ClerkSignIn()}` only when `currentView === "login" || !auth.signedIn`, so this subtree can unmount after auth state/route changes.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:1626-1628`: `{#snippet ClerkSignIn()}\n  <article class="paper-card clerk-card" use:mountClerk></article>\n{/snippet}` — the action is attached to the transient Clerk container.

`apps/app/node_modules/@clerk/clerk-js/dist/types/core/clerk.d.ts:103-104`: Clerk exposes the paired APIs `mountSignIn: (node: HTMLDivElement, props?: SignInProps) => void;` and `unmountSignIn: (node: HTMLDivElement) => void;`, but the app never calls `unmountSignIn`.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:34-72` defines a parallel registry: `type MutationName = keyof typeof mutationRefs;` and `const mutationRefs = { "users.onboarding.save": api.users.onboarding.save, ... } as const;`.
`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:458-459` queues only the string key: `function enqueueMutation(name: MutationName, args: AnyRecord) { writeQueue([...readQueue(), { name, args }]); }`.

`apps/app/src/components/OneRepApp.svelte:486-492` flushes by looking the string back up and stops on any failure: `await mutate(mutationRefs[item.name] as any, item.args as never); ... } catch { break; }`, so an unknown/stale `item.name` resolves to `undefined` and leaves that item at the head of `remaining`.
